missions.title: Five Days
missions.summary: Snow outside. Rent due in five days. A message from someone who wants to see what you're building.

on_start.text: Snow falling outside. A phone lights up.

message.text: Reminder: rent 9 400 SEK due in 5 days. Balance: 4 200 SEK.
Hey. Heard you're building something. Can you show me?

objectives.text: Reply to the message
Grab your laptop

on_complete.text: The unfinished product. A login screen and a scheduling grid that half works.

missions.title: Can You Show Me?
missions.summary: Customer discovery on foot across Södermalm and Gamla Stan.

objectives.text: Get to Kafé Kollektivet on Hornsgatan before 13:00

message.text: Had to leave for a supplier. Tomorrow, 8:30? Same place.

objectives.text: Meet Noor tomorrow at 08:30
Get to Kafé Kollektivet by 09:30

message.text: Okay. Come by when you're serious.

objectives.text: Go and apologise to Noor at the café
Talk to Noor
Walk to Kanel & Kod on Västerlånggatan, Gamla Stan
Show Aditi the prototype
Head home
Rework the prototype at your laptop

message.text: My friend Elin runs operations at Mälarbröd — twelve bakeries. Tomorrow 10:00, their office on Hantverkargatan, Kungsholmen. She won't wait.

missions.title: The First Pitch
missions.summary: Cross the city in a snowstorm to demo for a 12-bakery chain. The demo will fail. What you do next matters.

objectives.text: How will you get to Kungsholmen?
Catch Sami by his car as he gets home from his night shift
Drive to Mälarbröd on Hantverkargatan by 10:00
You're late. Get to Mälarbröd anyway
Get to Mälarbröd on Hantverkargatan by 10:00
You're late. Get to Mälarbröd anyway
Meet Elin Bergqvist
Start the live demo

on_complete.text: The office wifi drops. The rota grid freezes mid-render. Elin looks up.

objectives.text: The demo has frozen. Decide — now.

options.text: Switch to a manual walkthrough on a spreadsheet

objectives.text: Get the demo running again (offline cache, restart the sync)
Hear Elin's verdict
Fill the tank and return Sami's car by 20:00

message.text: Elin called me. Don't you dare celebrate before you invoice.

missions.recovery_hint: Losing Mälarbröd is not the end. Someone smaller may already believe in you.

missions.title: Another Door
missions.summary: A founders' breakfast, a stranger's advice, and the customer who was there all along.

message.text: Bad day? Founders' breakfast tomorrow 07:30, café on Strömgatan. Free cardamom buns. Go and talk to people.

objectives.text: Get to the founders' breakfast on Strömgatan by 09:30

on_fail.notify: The breakfast is over. Maybe the answer is closer to home.

objectives.text: Talk to the developer by the window
Go and see Noor
Talk to Noor

missions.recovery_hint: Noor is still at the café most days until 15:00.

missions.title: First Payment
missions.summary: Set a price, choose how to get paid, negotiate, and see real money arrive — just in time for rent, or not.

objectives.text: Write the proposal on your laptop
Set your price per location, per month

options.text: 2 900 SEK — what the pain is worth

objectives.text: How will you invoice?

options.text: Register as a sole trader (enskild firma) — cheap, personal liability
Form a limited company (aktiebolag) — needs 25 000 SEK share capital
Use an invoicing service — no registration, they keep 6 %

objectives.text: Take Elin's call about the proposal
Bring the proposal to Noor
Talk terms with Noor
Send the invoice from your laptop
Send the invoice from your laptop
Wait for the payment (tomorrow morning)
Rent: 9 400 SEK

options.text: Ask Gunilla for a week's grace

commit.text: Pay Gunilla the rent within 7 days
Pay Sami back 5 000 SEK within two weeks

message.text: First invoice paid. Write the date down. You'll want to remember it.

missions.recovery_hint: If you cannot pay rent, there are people who will help — at a cost to trust.

n1.speaker: noor
n1.text: Hey. Heard you're building something. Can you show me?

choices.text: Yes. Today. Where are you?
Who told you about it?
It's not ready yet...

n3a.speaker: noor
n3a.text: Kafé Kollektivet on Hornsgatan. I'm there until one. Bring whatever you have.

n3b.speaker: noor
n3b.text: Aditi. The baker in Gamla Stan who used to be a programmer. She says you don't sleep. Hornsgatan, before one?

n3c.speaker: noor
n3c.text: Nothing is ever ready. My first café opened with no sign. Hornsgatan, before one.

n1.speaker: noor
n1.text: You came. Sit. Coffee's on me, you look like you need it. So, what is it?

choices.text: Before I show you anything: what's the worst part of your week?
Let me show you the demo straight away.

n3_listen.speaker: noor
n3_listen.text: Sunday nights. I sit with three spreadsheets and twenty-two staff who all have exams, kids, second jobs. Then Monday someone's sick and it all falls apart.

n3_pitch.speaker: noor
n3_pitch.text: Mm. Lots of buttons. Every salesperson shows me buttons. What problem do you think I have?

choices.text: Honestly? I don't know yet. Tell me.
Scheduling. Every café has scheduling problems.

n3_guess.speaker: noor
n3_guess.text: Yes. Fine. Everyone says scheduling. Do you know how many staff I have? No. Twenty-two.

n4.speaker: noor
n4.text: And the bread. I order for a Saturday, it snows, nobody comes, I throw away two crates.

choices.text: How much does the waste cost you in a month?
If the schedule fixed itself when someone called in sick, what would that be worth?
My tool will fix all of that.

n6_waste.speaker: noor
n6_waste.text: Six, seven thousand kronor. More in January. Nobody talks about it because it's embarrassing.

n6_wtp.speaker: noor
n6_wtp.text: My Sunday evenings? More than my accountant charges. But it has to work every time. Once it fails on a Monday morning, I'm back to paper.

n6_over.speaker: noor
n6_over.text: All of it. Right. Let's start with one thing that works.

n7.speaker: noor
n7.text: Go and see Aditi at Kanel & Kod in Gamla Stan. She has the same problem, and she'll tell you if your code is rubbish. Then come back with something real.

choices.text: I'll have something you can try by Friday.

commit.text: Show Noor a working build by Friday

choices.text: Thank you. I'll come back when it's worth your time.

end.speaker: noor
end.text: Go. Before it gets dark at three.

n1.speaker: aditi
n1.text: Noor's founder! Come behind the counter, it's warmer. Show me what you've got. Code, not slides.

choices.text: Show her the scheduling prototype.
Show her everything at once.

n3.speaker: aditi
n3.text: The rota logic is clever. But you store shifts as strings? And if the wifi drops — which it does, in a 400-year-old cellar — the whole thing dies.

n3_all.speaker: aditi
n3_all.text: Slow down. Pick one thing. If I were Noor I'd want the rota. Also: it crashes without wifi. My cellar has no wifi.

choices.text: Would you pay for it if it worked offline?
Can you help me fix the offline problem?

n5_pay.speaker: aditi
n5_pay.text: Six hundred a month, maybe. For one shop. Noor has three; she'd pay more. Fix offline first.

n5_help.speaker: aditi
n5_help.text: Local-first. Queue changes on the device, sync when you can. I'll send you a link tonight. Don't tell my dough I said I miss programming.

message.text: Here's that article on local-first sync. Read the conflict-resolution part twice.

end.speaker: aditi
end.text: Take a cardamom bun. Founders forget to eat.

n1.speaker: sami
n1.text: Twelve hours on the ward. If you're here to borrow money, the answer is coffee.

choices.text: I need the Volvo. Real customer, Kungsholmen, ten o'clock.
How was the shift?

n2b.speaker: sami
n2b.text: Long. Someone's grandad made it, so — good. You want the car, don't you?

n3.speaker: sami
n3.text: Winter tyres are on. The heater only works on max. Back by eight tonight, full tank, or I'm taking the bus to work and you're hearing about it for a year.

choices.text: Back by eight. Full tank. Promise.

message.text: Took the bus to work. Thanks a lot.

end.speaker: sami
end.text: Go impress someone. Drive like my mum is watching.

n1.speaker: elin
n1.text: Noor says you listen. That's rare. I have twenty minutes.

n1_late.speaker: elin
n1_late.text: Everyone in Stockholm knows it snows in January. Now you have twelve minutes.

choices.text: Twelve bakeries means a lot of rota changes. How do you handle sick calls today?
choices.locked_hint: You don't know enough about their problem yet.

choices.text: We're building an AI platform for hospitality operations.

n3_good.speaker: elin
n3_good.text: A WhatsApp group with 140 people in it and a manager who cries on Mondays. Show me.

n3_buzz.speaker: elin
n3_buzz.text: So is everyone. Show me something that runs.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: Open the laptop to start the demo.

n1_late_apology.speaker: player
n1_late_apology.text: Sorry I'm late. The snow on Centralbron...

a1.speaker: elin
a1.text: You fixed that in front of me without panicking. That tells me more than the demo. Three bakeries, one month pilot. Paid — I don't do free; free means nobody cares.

a2.speaker: elin
a2.text: Send me pricing by tomorrow. Don't make me chase you.

b1.speaker: elin
b1.text: A spreadsheet. Honest, at least. The logic is right even if the software isn't. Send me a proposal by Thursday — with a date when offline mode works.

commit.text: Send Elin a proposal by Thursday

c1.speaker: elin
c1.text: I can't take this to the owners.

choices.text: You're right. The offline sync isn't there yet. Can I come back when it is?
It's just the office wifi. It works fine normally.

c3.speaker: elin
c3.text: Yes. People who say that usually don't come back. Prove me wrong.

c4.speaker: elin
c4.text: Our bakeries are in cellars and train stations. 'Normally' isn't a word I can use. Thank you for coming.

d1.speaker: elin
d1.text: Reschedule. Hm. My calendar is full until March. Send me an email when you have something stable.

n1.speaker: mateo
n1.text: You look like someone whose demo died yesterday. Sit — they have free cardamom buns and terrible coffee.

choices.text: It crashed. Twice. In front of a 12-bakery chain.
I'm fine. Just networking.

n3.speaker: mateo
n3.text: Big chains are slow anyway. Who already loves you? Start there. One small customer who pays beats twelve who are 'interested'.

n3b.speaker: mateo
n3b.text: Sure. Nobody comes here at 7:30 for fun. Who already likes what you're making?

n4.speaker: mateo
n4.text: Also — half the people in this room work out of the coworking spaces up the road. Put them on your map. That's where the founders are.

n1.speaker: noor
n1.text: Elin told me. She said you were honest. That's worth more to me than a demo.

n2.speaker: noor
n2.text: Here's my offer. My three cafés. You make Sunday nights disappear. I pay you. If it breaks on a Monday, you come here and fix it in person.

choices.text: Deal. I'll be here at 6:30 every Monday for a month.

commit.text: Be at Kafé Kollektivet at 06:30 on Mondays during the pilot

choices.text: Deal — but I can't promise in-person every week.

end.speaker: noor
end.text: Good. Now go home and write me a price. A real one.

n1.speaker: elin
n1.text: I read your proposal. Three bakeries. Before I sign: the owners want a discount, and finance asks if you'll take a free first month.

choices.text: Monthly, at the price I quoted. No discount — you'll see the value in week one.
Ten percent off if you pay the first quarter upfront.
Free first month, full price after.

n3_monthly.speaker: elin
n3_monthly.text: Confident. Fine. Invoice me the first month today.

n3_quarter.speaker: elin
n3_quarter.text: Finance will like that. I'll approve the quarter. Don't make me regret it.

n3_free.speaker: elin
n3_free.text: I told you I don't do free. But I'll take it. Invoice the 3 000 kronor setup fee, then we talk in a month.

end.speaker: narrator
end.text: Send the invoice from your laptop.

n1.speaker: noor
n1.text: I read it. Twice. It's fair. My accountant asks: monthly, or do I pay ahead for a discount?

choices.text: Monthly. If it doesn't work, you can walk.
Pay a quarter ahead, get ten percent off. It honestly helps me pay rent.
Try it free for a month. Just a small setup fee.

end.speaker: noor
end.text: Send me the invoice. I pay on time. Always.

warm.speaker: noor
warm.text: Cardamom or cinnamon? Don't answer, you look like cardamom.

cool.speaker: noor
cool.text: Friday came and went. I'm still here. Are you?

n1.speaker: aditi
n1.text: Tourists asked me today if the bakery is from the Viking age. I said yes. Business is business.

sore.speaker: sami
sore.text: The bus to the hospital takes fifty minutes, did you know? I know.

ok.speaker: sami
ok.text: You slept, right? Actually slept? Wellbeing is not a feature you ship later.

npcs.name: Noor Haddad
npcs.background: Came to Stockholm at nineteen to study hospitality management, washed dishes through school, and twelve years later runs three cafés on Södermalm. Keeps a paper notebook of every supplier she has ever fallen out with.
npcs.motivation: Sunday-night staff scheduling eats her weekends, and she throws out too much bread. She will pay for anything that gives her evenings back, but has been burned by software salespeople before.
npcs.appearance: 40s, practical wool coat, apron under it during the day, reading glasses on a cord

npcs.name: Sami Okafor
npcs.role: ICU nurse; your oldest friend in Stockholm
npcs.background: Grew up in Gothenburg, moved to Stockholm for nursing school and stayed. Rows on Riddarfjärden at dawn in summer, works rotating night shifts in winter. Owns a 2004 Volvo estate he loves more than is reasonable.
npcs.motivation: Saving for a deposit on his own flat. Worries you are trading your health for a dream; will help, but keeps score of borrowed things.
traits: keeps promises and expects the same
npcs.appearance: 30s, tall, scrubs under a puffer jacket, beanie

npcs.name: Aditi Rao
npcs.role: Baker, Kanel & Kod; former telecom software engineer
npcs.background: Spent nine years writing network software in Kista, then quit to open a bakery in Gamla Stan because she wanted to make something people could hold. Still reads code reviews for fun.
npcs.motivation: Wants her bakery to survive tourist low season. Misses building software more than she admits; could become an advisor or more.
npcs.appearance: late 30s, flour on sleeves, cardigan, smartwatch

npcs.name: Elin Bergqvist
npcs.role: Head of Operations, Mälarbröd (12 bakery cafés)
npcs.background: Former management consultant who joined a family-owned bakery chain to modernise it without losing what made it loved. Has bought, and cancelled, three software tools in two years.
npcs.motivation: Needs a win she can show the owners before the spring budget review. Values honesty over polish; remembers who wasted her time.
npcs.appearance: 40s, tailored dark coat, minimal jewellery, tablet always in hand

npcs.name: Gunilla Ek
npcs.role: First-hand tenant subletting you the room
npcs.background: Retired school librarian who sublets her spare room while she spends winters with her daughter in Umeå. Has had bad lodgers; hopes you are not one.
npcs.motivation: Needs the rent on time to cover her own costs. Not unkind, but cannot afford to be patient for long.
npcs.appearance: 70, reading glasses, phone held at arm's length

npcs.name: Mateo Ruiz
npcs.role: Backend developer between jobs; potential co-founder
npcs.background: Moved from Montevideo for a fintech job that evaporated in a reorg. Codes in cafés in Norrmalm while deciding whether to stay in Sweden.
npcs.motivation: Wants to build something that matters and needs a residence-permit-safe path to do it. Will join a founder who is honest about risk.
npcs.appearance: late 20s, headphones, oversized hoodie under a parka

npcs.name: Helena Sjöberg
npcs.role: Angel investor; sold her logistics software company in 2019
npcs.background: Built and sold a fictional route-planning company after eleven hard years. Now writes small cheques and gives large amounts of uncomfortable advice. Appears from Chapter 3.
npcs.motivation: Wants to back founders who listen to customers. Cares about control terms more than valuation headlines.
npcs.appearance: 50s, silver hair, sneakers with a suit

districts.name: Gamla Stan
districts.description: Medieval old town on Stadsholmen: narrow lanes, tourism, Royal Palace waterfront, Skeppsbron quay.

districts.name: Norrmalm
districts.description: Commercial centre: Sergels torg, Drottninggatan, Kungsträdgården, Central Station. Coworking and startup offices.

districts.name: Södermalm
districts.description: Island of apartments, cafés, creative communities and nightlife. The player's first home is here. Milestone A covers the northern edge (Slussen–Mariatorget–Hornsgatan).

districts.name: Kungsholmen
districts.description: Residential island with long waterfront walks; City Hall at its eastern tip. Milestone A covers the eastern tip only.

districts.name: Östermalm / Stureplan
districts.description: High-end business life, investor offices, networking dinners and events around Stureplan and Birger Jarlsgatan.

districts.name: Vasastan

districts.name: KTH / Valhallavägen

districts.name: Kista

districts.name: Solna

entries.name: Spotify
entries.summary: Music streaming service founded in Stockholm in April 2006. It went public on 3 April 2018 through a direct listing on the New York Stock Exchange, without raising new capital. Wikipedia reports over 788 million monthly active users (306 million paying subscribers) as of March 2026. Since 1 January 2026 Daniel Ek has been executive chairman, with Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström serving as co-CEOs.

status.label: public
status.detail: Listed on NYSE since the April 2018 direct listing. Spotify AB is headquartered in Stockholm.

unicorn.note: Was a private unicorn before 2018; publicly listed since April 2018.

storyline_hooks: Licensing gauntlet: get rights holders to sign before the launch window closes.
Freemium economics: convert free users to paying ones without driving the free users away.
Leadership handover: a founder moves up to chairman and the team must keep shipping.

sources.title: Harvard Law School Forum: Spotify direct listing case study
NPR: Daniel Ek to step aside as CEO (2025-09-30)

entries.notes: The listed entity is Spotify Technology S.A. (Luxembourg). Wikipedia describes the listing as American depositary receipts; it is recorded here only as 'NYSE: SPOT'. The office is in the 'Urban Escape' block, per the Spotify newsroom.

entries.name: Klarna
entries.summary: Payments and 'buy now, pay later' company founded in Stockholm in 2005 (originally Kreditor Europe AB) after its founders took part in the Stockholm School of Economics entrepreneurship competition. It created a UK holding company (Klarna Group plc, incorporated in England and Wales) in 2023–24, ahead of an IPO. Klarna listed on the NYSE on 10 September 2025 at $40 per share (about $15B valuation). The share price later fell well below the IPO price. Q3 2026 revenue was about $1.01B, with a net loss of $65M.

status.label: public
status.detail: NYSE-listed since September 2025 through Klarna Group plc (England and Wales). The operating bank, Klarna Bank AB (publ), keeps its registered head office in Stockholm.

unicorn.note: Was one of Europe's most valuable private fintechs before the IPO; public since September 2025.

locations.label: Klarna Bank AB registered and head office

storyline_hooks: Trust problem: persuade shoppers and merchants that a new checkout is safe.
Credit-loss squeeze: grow lending volume without letting defaults eat the margin.
Going public: restructure the holding company and survive the share price after the IPO.

sources.title: Fortune: Klarna jumps in NYSE debut (2025-09-11)
CNBC: Klarna sets up UK holding company (2023-11-06)
The Next Web: Klarna Q3 2026 results

entries.notes: Some finance sites list Klarna as 'based in London' because of the UK plc. The Stockholm address is the head office of Klarna Bank AB. Share-price figures move constantly and are deliberately left out of the summary.

entries.name: King (Candy Crush)
entries.summary: Mobile and social game maker founded in Stockholm in August 2003 as Midasplayer.com and renamed King.com in 2005. It rose to fame with Candy Crush Saga (2012). Activision Blizzard bought it for $5.9B, closing in February 2016. Microsoft completed its purchase of Activision Blizzard on 13 October 2023, so King is now part of Microsoft's Xbox. In July 2025 it cut about 10% of its staff (around 200 jobs), mostly in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Part of Microsoft (Xbox), via Activision Blizzard. Wikipedia: headquartered in Stockholm and London, incorporated in Malta.

unicorn.note: Went public in 2014 at a valuation of around $7B. No longer independent.

storyline_hooks: Near-bankruptcy: keep a browser-game startup alive until a hit arrives.
One-hit risk: follow up a mega-hit casual game.
Corporate parent: keep a studio's culture after two acquisitions in a row.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Activision Blizzard closes $5.9B acquisition of King (2016-02-23)
Microsoft blog: welcoming Activision Blizzard King (2023-10-13)

entries.notes: The Sveavägen 44 address comes from 2015 architecture coverage. Whether King is still there in 2026 is unconfirmed, so it is marked historical. The founder list follows the Wikipedia infobox as reported in search results; other sources omit some names.

entries.name: Mojang Studios (Minecraft)
entries.summary: Game studio founded in Stockholm in 2009 by Markus Persson around Minecraft. Mojang AB was incorporated in 2010. Microsoft announced the purchase on 15 September 2014 for $2.5B and completed it on 6 November 2014. Today Mojang Studios is an Xbox studio based in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Xbox studio owned by Microsoft since November 2014.

unicorn.note: Acquired for $2.5B in 2014; not independent since.

storyline_hooks: Indie breakout: a side project goes viral and has to become a company overnight.
Selling the studio: decide whether to sell a beloved game to a platform giant.

sources.title: Microsoft News: Minecraft to join Microsoft (2014-09-15)
Engadget: Microsoft completes acquisition of Minecraft studio (2014-11-06)

entries.notes: Sources give different founding dates (May or June 2009; incorporation in September 2010). The Söder Mälarstrand 43 address was seen only via Wikipedia and aggregator search snippets, not on a Mojang page. A fan wiki names Maria Skolgata 83 as an earlier office (unconfirmed, not recorded). Other co-founders are left out because no source seen named them.

entries.name: Skype
entries.founded_in: Registered in Luxembourg; software developed in Tallinn (Swedish and Danish founders)
entries.summary: Internet calling service founded in 2003 by Swede Niklas Zennström and Dane Janus Friis. The software was written by Estonian engineers (Ahti Heinla, Priit Kasesalu and Jaan Tallinn). The company was registered in Luxembourg and had offices including Tallinn and Stockholm. Microsoft completed its $8.5B acquisition on 13 October 2011. Microsoft retired the consumer Skype service on 5 May 2025 and moved users to Teams Free.

status.label: defunct
status.detail: Consumer service retired by Microsoft on 5 May 2025. Users were migrated to Microsoft Teams Free.

unicorn.note: Acquired by Microsoft for $8.5B in 2011; the service no longer runs.

storyline_hooks: Peer-to-peer scaling: run a global calling network on a startup budget.
Legacy sunset: migrate millions of users when a parent company retires a product.

sources.title: Microsoft News: Microsoft officially welcomes Skype (2011-10-13)
TechCrunch: Skype to shut down May 5, 2025

entries.notes: Skype is only loosely a 'Stockholm' company: one co-founder is Swedish and it had a Stockholm office, but it was registered in Luxembourg and engineered in Tallinn. No Stockholm street address was found. district is 'other' (unknown). Present it in-game as a historical landmark, not a current company.

entries.name: Zettle by PayPal (formerly iZettle)
entries.summary: Mobile card-reader and point-of-sale company founded in Stockholm in April 2010. It launched its first app and chip-card reader in 2011. PayPal agreed to buy iZettle in May 2018, cancelling a planned IPO, and completed the roughly $2.2B deal on 20 September 2018. The company renamed itself 'Zettle by PayPal' in February 2021.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Owned by PayPal since September 2018, trading as Zettle by PayPal.

unicorn.note: Acquired for about $2.2B in 2018 (PayPal's largest deal at the time).

storyline_hooks: Hardware plus software: ship a card reader small merchants trust on day one.
IPO or exit: choose between listing and selling to a payments giant.

sources.title: PayPal newsroom: PayPal completes acquisition of iZettle (2018-09-20)
Zettle: iZettle is now Zettle by PayPal

entries.notes: CB Insights lists 'Regeringsgatan 59, Stockholm', but that is an aggregator, so the location is kept at city precision. The Wikipedia HQ sentence is marked 'citation needed'. No 2025–2026 status change was found.

entries.name: Tink
entries.summary: Open-banking platform founded in Stockholm in 2012. It connects to more than 3,400 banks across Europe. Visa announced the deal in June 2021 (about €1.8B) and completed it on 10 March 2022; Visa's filings report about $1.9B in cash. Tink runs as a standalone Visa subsidiary, and Visa said its headquarters would stay in Stockholm.

status.label: subsidiary
status.detail: Wholly owned subsidiary of Visa since March 2022.

unicorn.note: Acquired by Visa in 2022 for about €1.8B.

storyline_hooks: Bank integrations: connect to thousands of banks, each with its own quirks.
Regulatory clock: build a product around a new open-banking rule.

sources.title: Visa IR: Visa completes acquisition of Tink (2022-03-10)
